title: Run A/B tests and experiments
summary: An A/B test shows two versions to similar groups of users and compares results. It is the most reliable way to know whether a change caused an improvement.

beginner: Write a hypothesis: what you will change, for whom, and what you expect to happen.
Pick one main metric and one or two guardrails before you start.
Ask an analyst how many users and how long you need for a reliable answer.
Split users at random between the current version and the new one.
Do not stop early because the result looks good. Wait until the planned end.
Record the result, including when nothing changed, and decide what to do next.
intermediate: Write a hypothesis with a primary metric and guardrails.
Calculate sample size and duration before starting.
Run the test without peeking or changing it midway.
Analyse, record and share the result.
experienced: Run an A/A test or sample checks to make sure the experiment system is trustworthy.
Use an overall evaluation measure that reflects long-term value.
Watch for novelty effects and differences between user groups.
Build an experiment log so the organisation learns from every test.

canDelegateTo.task: Design the test, calculate sample size and analyse results
Build the variants behind a feature flag

toolExamples.amplitude: Use the experiment features to assign users and analyse results with guardrails.
toolExamples.mixpanel: Use the experiments report to compare variants on your main metric.
toolExamples.ga4: Compare variant audiences on key events if you run tests through another tool.
toolExamples.notion: Keep an experiment log: hypothesis, design, result and decision.

definitionOfDone: Hypothesis, metric and guardrails set before starting
pitfalls: Stopping early when the result looks good
Testing many changes at once and not knowing which worked
